## GREEN — the feed is keyed to the hardware that ships; the release re-drove and verified

**The fix**: `a439a15` — CI 13/13 (run 42820611361).

1. **The manifest builder learned the real v2 shapes** (the run-42816215486 log wire fact: v2's `createUpdaterArtifacts` signs the INSTALLERS — `.deb.sig`/`.AppImage.sig`/`.rpm.sig`/`.exe.sig`/`.msi.sig` — and wraps only macOS in `.app.tar.gz`; the v1 wrapper bundles the old code globed and fixtured never occur): linux → the `.AppImage`, windows → the NSIS `.exe` (passive install, `.msi` fallback), macOS → the `.app.tar.gz` under the **DECLARED** `--darwin-arch` (the name carries no arch; an undeclared one fails `UNKEYED` instead of guessing — the guess WAS the defect).
2. **The collector ships the installer `.sig` sidecars** — the pairing rule (no signature, no entry) can now actually see them; the sidecars also joined the attestation subjects and the verify gate.
3. **The detector rides every release**: the publish leg runs the self-test (now fixtured on the run-log artifacts, not the v1 fiction the old test named — a gate that tested a story, not the wire) BEFORE building the real manifest. Publish log of the re-drive: `SELF-TEST PASS: v2 pairing, platform map, NSIS preference, schema` → `latest.json written: release_assets/latest.json (3 platforms)`.

**The re-drive**: tag v0.2.1 moved to `a439a15`, release run 42821542083 SUCCESS; the asset set re-collected (33 assets — six installers, seven `.sig` sidecars, two SBOMs, SHA256SUMS, latest.json, every subject attested). One wrinkle handled on the record: deleting the tag to move it flipped the existing release to DRAFT (GitHub's documented behavior); re-published via the API before verification — the release body, sizes table and checksums are the workflow's own output.

**Verified before declared (receipts, not vibes):**

- the published `latest.json` (downloaded, not assumed): `darwin-aarch64 → IUM.app.tar.gz`, `linux-x86_64 → IUM_0.2.1_amd64.AppImage`, `windows-x86_64 → IUM_0.2.1_x64-setup.exe` — every shipped OS/arch has an entry whose URL is a real asset;
- the manifest's `darwin-aarch64` signature **byte-identical** to the published `IUM.app.tar.gz.sig` asset (decoded both layers of base64 and compared — the first comparison that said False was my own layer confusion, corrected here on the record);
- the key map was simulated locally on the real v0.2.1 artifact names before the push.

The v0.2.0 → v0.2.1 Apple-Silicon update check now resolves: newer feed → entry found for `darwin-aarch64` → signed bundle → minisign verifies against the pubkey in `tauri.conf.json`. Windows joins the updater at the next version bump with a real entry; Linux serves the AppImage. USERGUIDE §8's Windows-passive sentence is true as written. The manual install-over path (verified in the release smoke legs) stays the honest fallback everywhere.
